brief: Raymond James's post-midterm daily recap links several stories. First, the S&P 500's 1.6% rally the day after the midterms was the second-strongest post-midterm first-session gain since 1982, consistent with a historical pattern (positive 72% of the time since 1930); RJ frames this as markets cheering reduced uncertainty from a clear election outcome, with Consumer Discretionary and Financials leading and Energy lagging on lower oil. Second, hyperscaler stocks rallied even as new state governors may tighten data-center rules, because RJ argues slower new builds would shift the AI bottleneck from chip supply to existing compute capacity, which hyperscalers dominate, also easing capex and balance-sheet pressure. Third, divided government leaves room for narrow bipartisan deals (energy permitting, defense spending) but a $1.5t FY27 budget request is unlikely to pass. Fourth, strong ADP and JOLTS data support a healthy-labor-market view ahead of Friday's payrolls (RJ forecasts +70k, unemployment at 4.2%). Fifth, WTI fell 8% on signs of US-Iran dialogue and a Vance social-media post read as dovish, though RJ cautions no durable settlement exists yet.
